importantTopics: Basics of Optimization and Feasible Regions
likelyQuestions: Explain the fundamental components of an optimization problem, giving examples of decision variables and constraints.
Define feasible regions and explain how boundedness affects the existence of an optimal solution with an illustrative example.
Give at least four real-world applications where optimization techniques are critical for operational efficiency.
Consider a set of n points in a 2D plane. Formulate a nonlinear optimization problem to find a point minimizing the sum of absolute distances (L1 norm) to all other points.
Discuss the differentiability and convexity of the objective function when minimizing the sum of Euclidean distances to a set of given points.
State the necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for unconstrained convex optimization problems, clearly stating any required assumptions.
Provide a semidefinite programming formulation for minimizing the maximum Euclidean distance from a point to a given set of points.
A manufacturing firm produces multiple products under regular and overtime constraints with varying profit margins. Formulate this resource allocation problem as a linear programming model.
Formulate an optimization problem for decision making under uncertainty where demand can take one of two discrete values with known probabilities, subject to a strict budget constraint.
Analyze the qualitative outcomes of a decision-making model under budget constraints when the maximum versus minimum expected demand scenarios occur.
